findings.title: `source_bar_stamping` accepts a plain `str`, unlike every other enum-typed field
findings.description: `Market.__post_init__` validates `source_bar_stamping` by membership in `SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` (a `frozenset` of `TimeMeaning` members, `markets.py:48-50`). Because `TimeMeaning` is a `StrEnum`, `TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START == "period_start"` and `hash(TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START) == hash("period_start")`, so the set membership test succeeds for the raw string and `Market(source_bar_stamping="period_start", ...)` is accepted, storing a plain `str` in a field declared `TimeMeaning`. This is inconsistent with every other enum-typed field in the same slice: `continuity_kind` (`markets.py:102-104`) and `SessionCalendarRef.session_mode` (`markets.py:64-66`) both go through `_require_instance`, which rejects a plain string, and `markets.py:94` is the only place that does not. The gap is visible in the test table too: `tests/core_model/test_markets.py:123` has a `("non-enum continuity", ...)` row but no equivalent row for a non-`TimeMeaning` `source_bar_stamping`, so nothing pins the stricter behaviour. The consequence is a latent runtime fault at the boundary slice 140 is meant to consume ("140's availability function reads it"): `market.source_bar_stamping.value` raises `AttributeError` on a plain `str`, and `market.source_bar_stamping is TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START` silently evaluates to `False` because `StrEnum` equality is by value, not identity. Suggested fix: call `_require_instance(self.source_bar_stamping, TimeMeaning, "market.source_bar_stamping")` before the membership check, and add the missing rejection row to `REJECTED_MARKETS`.

findings.title: Duplicated `_require_instance` helper in two modules
findings.description: `_require_instance` is duplicated verbatim in `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/instruments.py:80-86` and `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/markets.py:132-140`; the only difference is which error class is raised (`InvalidInstrumentError` vs `InvalidMarketError`). AGENTS.md asks for DRY, and a single shared helper parameterized by the error type would live naturally in `errors.py`, which both modules already import (so the dependency direction `errors ← ... ← markets ← instruments` in the slice design is preserved). Not a blocker, but the duplication will grow as more validation helpers are added.

findings.title: Dead constant `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS` in the uniformity test
findings.description: `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS = 60_000_000_000` is defined but never referenced anywhere in the repository (the test derives the width via `BarSpec.time(60)` at `tests/core_model/test_market_uniformity.py:56`, and the expected ends are written as separate literals). It is both dead code and a second, unreferenced copy of the 60-second width — exactly the kind of scattered comparison value AGENTS.md warns about. Deleting it, or using it to derive the expected end literals, would remove the ambiguity.

findings.title: `EQUITY_EXTENDED_FIXTURE` literals match their documented New York wall times
findings.description: I recomputed all nine session opens/closes and both coverage bounds from the local wall times in the comments using the EDT (UTC-4) boundary on 2026-11-01 and EST (UTC-5) after it: 04:00 EDT = 08:00 UTC, 20:00 EDT = 24:00 UTC, 04:00 EST = 09:00 UTC, 20:00 EST = 01:00 UTC next day, and the 2026-11-05 early close at 17:00 EST = 22:00 UTC. Every literal matches, the 16-hour session length stays within `MAX_TIME_BAR_WIDTH_NS`, and the session dates match `EQUITY_RTH_FIXTURE` exactly (including the 2026-11-04 holiday and the unknown 2026-10-30 close), as the design requires.

findings.title: Byte-pinned golden rows follow 101's canonical encoding rules
findings.description: I derived the expected bytes for both new byte-pinned rows by hand from `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/canonical.py`: the `SessionCalendarRef` row sorts `$schema`/`$type` before the field keys and encodes the `StrEnum` as its string value, and the `ContractTerms` row sorts to `currency`/`lot_size`/`multiplier`/`tick_size`, uses `{"$dec":"1"}` / `{"$dec":"50"}` for the decimals (trailing zeros stripped, exponent folded) and `{"$unknown":true}` for the unknown tick. Both agree with the literals in the file, and the two byte-pinned rows are genuinely independent of `canonical_hash` output.

findings.title: Package-wide canonical and import guards are enforced mechanically
findings.description: `EXPECTED_MODULES` is extended with all four new modules, `test_market_and_instrument_types_keep_their_boundary` asserts mechanically that neither `markets.py` nor `instruments.py` imports `calendars`, `canonical` or any `fixtures` module, and `test_module_imports_stay_inside_boundary` is parametrized over `rglob("*.py")`, so the new files are scanned rather than trusted. `tests/core_model/test_canonical_types.py:47-63` extends the package walk to require the four new type ids and to assert every collected id stays in the `core.` namespace, so a later slice cannot silently introduce a colliding id.
